pos.personaBrief: Gap axis, no verified possession evidence, so this rests on general knowledge: Sebes's Golden Team built its play on fluid passing and collective movement (FIFA, undated 'socialist football' label), so the ball is valued for attack and control, but the side was not a slow possession team that held the ball for its own sake.

pro.personaBrief: Gap axis, general knowledge only: the Hidegkuti-led attack progressed through short passing and drop-off movement (UEFA, verified: 'deep-lying centre-forward ... draw defenders out of position'), so patient build-up is preferred, while the side still struck quickly on the counter.

est.personaBrief: Verified (UEFA, Wikipedia): the 4-2-4 used a deep-lying centre-forward who dropped into midfield while Puskas and Kocsis took space, and tactical discussions were regular with the captain's input, so the shape was drilled but roles were fluid and interchangeable.

lar.personaBrief: Gap axis, general knowledge only: the 4-2-4 kept wingers, but the verified facts show the attacks were built through the centre with Hidegkuti and Puskas, so the middle is the main route while the flanks remain a secondary option.

blo.personaBrief: Gap axis, general knowledge only: no verified pressing or block evidence was read. The verified in-game switch to Hidegkuti when 2-0 down to Switzerland in 1952 (Wikipedia) points to a team that changes and attacks rather than sitting deep, so the answers lean to a high, active side without relying on a verified press.

mar.personaBrief: Gap axis, general knowledge only: the verified Hidegkuti move was designed to pull defenders out of position, which implies opponents marked tightly and Sebes exploited it, so the team gains from movement against man-marking and treats zonal space as useful.

pla.personaBrief: Verified: Sebes kept the team's own collective style ('socialist football', FIFA) yet changed it in-game (Hidegkuti in for Palotas in 1952 at 2-0 down, Wikipedia) and prepared for specific conditions (Wembley-sized training pitch and heavier balls in 1953, Wikipedia), so the identity is kept but the game is adjusted to the match.

res.personaBrief: Verified: the team won the 1952 Olympics and reached the 1954 World Cup final with an attacking, technical style (Wikipedia, FIFA), so winning mattered but the football was part of the purpose, and it did not settle for draws or shut games down late.

sis.personaBrief: Verified: the Golden Team was built as a collective, with a defined tactical plan and roles even for the stars (Hidegkuti's role was set by Sebes, Wikipedia; regular tactical discussions, UEFA), so the system is the frame and the talent works inside it.

jog.personaBrief: Gap axis, general knowledge only: the Golden Team combined technique with fitness (heavy training, Wembley preparation, Wikipedia), so technique and organisation were prioritised over physical duels, with stamina a requirement rather than the main selection criterion.

bas.personaBrief: Verified: Sebes 'did away with the established stars' soon after taking charge in 1949 (UEFA), bringing in newer players, so youth and form were preferred over reputation, but the title-winning squad still relied on experienced core players such as Puskas.

lid.personaBrief: Verified: the captain's input shaped tactical discussions (UEFA), so the coach listened to his best player, yet the coach set the rules and the structure, and the group's discipline was tight, so the leadership is firm and inclusive at once.
